title: Network lab 3: DNS, a web server and a fault to find (Filius)
summary: Add a web server and a DNS server, open the shop's site by name, then troubleshoot a computer that can't, one layer at a time.

script.intro: Today the network gets names and a website, and then a fault you have to find the way a help desk does: one layer at a time.
script.outro: When something can't connect, test from the bottom up: link, address, gateway, DNS, then the service.
steps: Today the network gets names and a website, and then a fault you have to find the way a help desk does: one layer at a time.

Set every computer's DNS server to 192.168.2.53. On till-1, install Web browser and open http://www.banyan.lan. Then open Show data exchange on till-1 and find the DNS question before the web request.
Go to design mode and break till-2 in one way: change its gateway to 192.168.1.100. Now pretend you don't know. On till-2, work up the layers and write what each test shows:
Names, a service, and a calm, bottom-up way to find faults. The Packet Tracer labs move to real switch and router commands, starting with VLANs.
